rows.title: The city of Suslanger and its environs

versions.html:
Suslanger

Setting

Suslanger is a dry Khadaganian allod with little cultivable land. A river, lake, dams and irrigation channels sustain its settlements. Imperial decrees are enforced by guards and informers. Beyond that order lie necromancers’ laboratories, Wormface caverns and the hidden refuge of escaped slaves. [1, 2, 3]

Tka-Rik’s warning about Suslanger

Before Zak leaves for Suslanger, Tka-Rik describes the Khadaganian hierarchy, in which even a master is subject to someone above him. Emperor Neseb is himself a powerful magician. Suslanger is a provincial backwater, but that does not make it safe. The old Joon portal provides a route there; informants and imperial attention make open enquiries about the missing Joon dangerous. [4, 5]

Captivity in Death Canyon

Zak is captured near the portal on Suslanger. Lieutenant Kardaur presents him to Aiset-Bek, who orders him used as live quarry for soldiers seeking promotion. Surviving the run through Death Canyon earns only a return to captivity, not freedom. Kardaur threatens punishment through necromancy if Zak dies too quickly and displeases his superior. [6, 7]

The Odalisque and the escape

The Odalisque approaches Zak after his ordeal. Enslaved by Kardaur and deprived even of a personal name, she wants his death and knows he will guard the gate that night. She steals the key to Zak’s cage. Her father, a rat hunter who disappeared in the caves, told her of the Wormheads’ temple and the bridges across its lava rivers. She uses that knowledge to explain a route the guards fear to follow. Zak kills Kardaur for the fortress key and escapes toward the cave; releasing the caged spiders can delay pursuit. The Odalisque and Zak part with wishes for each other’s freedom and survival, without a stated account of her later fate. [8, 9, 10, 11, 12]

Acceptance into the Last Shelter

Beyond the caves, Brother Blacksmith finds Zak and vouches for him before Brother Khatul. The brotherhood’s leader fears imperial spies and requires the Emperor’s Signet Ring, taken from a cyclops who killed its courier. Possessing such an object compromises the newcomer with the authorities and makes the test more than a feat of strength. After Zak returns, Khatul accepts him as Brother Blondie and offers the refuge as a new home. Zak explains his promise to find At-Zako and return to Gipath. Khatul respects that purpose and asks those who can help to support him; Brother Blind can teach him greater dexterity. [13, 14, 15]

The Blacksmith’s revenge and Kehel’s experiment

The Shelter’s inhabitants can ask for help with their own grievances alongside the search for At-Zako. Brother Blacksmith wants the slavedriver brothers Lash-Aga and Whip-Aga killed at the plantations. If Zak carries out the request, the workers raise the alarm instead of helping him. The smith explains that imperial law threatens them with death if they fail to report a stranger, then promises to repay the revenge. Kehel offers a separate commission: destroy a harpy he once experimented on, so rivals cannot claim his work. After its death, he admits that fear of Zak’s strength is what makes him honour the promised reward. Their requests expose different consequences of life under the empire: coerced obedience among the workers, personal revenge among its fugitives, and rivalry among its scholars. [16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21]

Sahilia’s cache and the Joon collector

Sahilia supplies the next lead through her own theft. Antiquities she stole from Baluddin remain hidden near the city, and Zak recovers them to arrange a meeting. Khatul and Brother Blacksmith help choose the secluded trading place, keeping strangers away from the Shelter. Baluddin admits recognising At-Zako as a living Joon and wanting to keep him in his own house. Imperial scholars took the young man away. Later, Taivo summoned the collector to identify those scholars’ mutilated bodies. The missing youth’s trail now leads to the necromancers rather than a living prisoner whom Zak can simply rescue. [22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28]

Kholai and the dead scientist

Kehel directs Zak to Kholai, whom Taivo displaced from the imperial laboratory. Kholai wants disgrace for his rival rather than a simple assassination. Zak steals a dead scientist’s head from the laboratory; its disappearance will embarrass Taivo, and Kholai can summon its spirit. The scientist describes a horror pursuing the red-skinned youth. To conceal him, the scholars changed his appearance and sent him away by teleportation. Kholai interprets the broken testimony and tells Zak to search the ruined mansion for the magical object used in the escape. The fragments Zak finds are beyond Kehel’s ability to interpret: only a Great Magician can identify the destination. Kholai can also give Zak an experimental object to test in combat. He is interested in the result even if the trial kills its user, a further sign of the limits of his concern for his visitor. [29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36]

Brother Faceless and the return to Gipath

Khatul asks Brother Faceless to help Zak reach the guarded portal. Faceless arranges a cave meeting and explains the keys and stone controls. He then reveals himself as Erfar: born on Suslanger, he went to Gipath seeking the meteorite and manipulated the villagers into searching for it. His earlier plots were attempts to remove Zak, who disrupted that scheme. The reunion is another trap, with guards waiting outside the cave. Zak survives the confrontation and forces a route through the portal’s defences. Activating its two controls finally returns him to Tka-Rik with the amulet fragments. [37, 38, 39, 40, 41]
